title: Domestic orientation and the reach of any court
shortTitle: Domestic orientation and the reach of any court
summary: A domestic-orientation assumption treats a statute as addressing domestic institutions or conduct unless the relevant context indicates otherwise.
notes:
Small applies this assumption to the class of predicate convictions used in a domestic gun-possession offense. The majority analogizes to the presumption against extraterritorial application, but the immediate question concerns a prior foreign judgment’s consequences in domestic law. It examines text, exceptions, purpose, and practical difficulties of judging foreign convictions.

Thomas objects that the assumption lacks justification against the unqualified phrase any court. The case therefore should not be summarized as a dictionary establishing that any excludes foreign entities, or as a holding that Congress lacks power to count foreign convictions. It is a contested contextual construction of a particular provision.
